title: Disjoint union of two proper schemes over a base is proper
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $p_1:W_1\to S$ and $p_2:W_2\to S$ morphisms of schemes, $W=W_1\amalg W_2$ the disjoint union (coproduct in the category of schemes) with coprojections $\iota_1:W_1\to W$, $\iota_2:W_2\to W$, and $p:W\to S$ the morphism with $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$ ($k=1,2$). (1) $\iota_1$ and $\iota_2$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and the underlying set of $W$ is the disjoint union of $\iota_1(W_1)$ and $\iota_2(W_2)$. (2) If $p_1$ and $p_2$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then $p$ is proper.

proof.text: The two coprojections are open immersions and have complementary ranges by the binary instances and isCompl_range_inl_inr in Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Limits (the binary specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]). This gives the first three conjuncts.

Assume both component maps proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Mathlib IsProper is Zariski-local at the target. Apply IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.coprodMap to p1 and p2: the map W1 coproduct W2 to S coproduct S is proper, since its restrictions over the two complementary target opens are the two given proper maps. The locality instance is in Morphisms/Proper.lean:77 and coprodMap in Morphisms/Basic.lean:207.

The identities of S are finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct], the fold map coprod.desc (identity S) (identity S) from S coproduct S to S is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Compose it with the proper coproduct map using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. The composite equals coprod.desc p1 p2 by coproduct extensionality and the coprojection equations, finishing the last conjunct.
